summary: When the first meaningful sequence is empty, all n values from nums2 must be written into nums1, giving a linear output lower bound. The current backward merge performs at most m+n writes and matches it.

optimality.argument: Choose the legal family m = 0 and n > 0. The reserved positions in nums1 are placeholders, so every one of the n = m + n meaningful values from nums2 must be copied into nums1; producing the required in-place result therefore takes Omega(m+n) writes. In the current algorithm, each loop iteration writes one unmerged value and decrements either first or second. There can be at most m + n iterations, yielding O(m+n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: For m = 0, every nums1 position is reserved capacity and all n source values must be materialized there, requiring n = m + n writes.
Each iteration fixes one destination position and consumes one endpoint; neither first nor second can be decremented more than its source length.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover interleaving, an empty nums2, and an empty meaningful nums1 prefix; black-box real-test execution verifies all existing ordinary checks without inspecting their definitions.
